name: Axiom Systems Memory Crystal Archive MCA-4
product_name: Axiom Systems Memory Crystal Archive MCA-4
description: A portable holographic data storage device using Tessera crystal technology in an Axiom-designed security housing. The MCA-4 stores up to 500 petabytes of data in a device the size of a large coin, protected by biometric lock and quantum encryption. If tampered with, the crystal's data can be scrambled in microseconds, destroying the information before it can be extracted. Axiom uses the MCA-4 for field data storage during intelligence operations — an entire corporation's data archive fits in a device that can be swallowed.
story_hooks: An MCA-4 was recovered from a dead operative's stomach — the crystal survived digestion and its data is intact, but the biometric lock requires the dead person's neural interface signature to open.

An MCA-4 has been found pre-loaded with data that does not match any known source — the crystal contains what appears to be a comprehensive map of GLMZ's underground infrastructure, including facilities that officially do not exist.

physical_description.visual_profile: A precision-engineered coin-sized disc with a jewel-like center that shifts between deep indigo and teal under light. The Tessera crystal at its core is visible through a transparent security window, suspended in a gossamer suspension field that creates subtle chromatic aberrations. The device has an almost biological elegance despite its industrial housing.
physical_description.dimensions: 3 cm diameter, 0.8 cm thickness — fits in the palm of a hand or between two fingers
physical_description.weight_description: Feather-light at 10 grams; pocketable, easily swallowable in emergency protocols
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium-ceramic composite housing with polycarbonate crystal view port
physical_description.finish: Satin gunmetal with brushed micro-texturing to reduce fingerprints; holographic rainbow fleck pattern across the rim that catches light
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal grey housing with the central Tessera crystal displaying an opalescent indigo-to-teal gradient. Axiom branding in discrete metallic silver. Small biometric scanner ring in matte black.
physical_description.interface_elements: Miniature holographic contact points (visible only when powered); neural interface port recessed into bottom surface; secondary fingerprint scanner ring around the perimeter; tiny status LED (green idle, amber reading, red tamper alert) embedded flush in upper edge
distinctive_features: Visible Tessera crystal suspended in micro-field within transparent window — appears to float
Holographic shimmer across the device's rim that pulses faintly when active
Biometric scanner ring that glows faint amber during authentication
Aerospace-precision tolerances visible in panel seams and port edges
Axiom Systems corporate security hologram etched into bottom — only visible under specific light angle
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS text in minimalist serif font on upper face; MCA-4 designation below; regulatory stamps for GLMZ Tier 4+ clearance; microscopic serial number laser-etched inside crystal view port
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine, as field operatives maintain obsessive care; often observed being handled with microfiber cloth; frequently paired with discrete wrist-mounted neural interface jack
